rci1_using_msad.detail: Multi-site; 6 sites: Cambridge (UK), King's College London (UK), Mannheim (Germany), Nijmegen (Netherlands), Rome (Italy), Utrecht (Netherlands)
rci1_using_msad.supporting_text: "All participants were scanned with a 3T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanner at 6 different sites: Cambridge, United Kingdom (Siemens Verio); London, United Kingdom (General Electric Discovery mr750); Mannheim, Germany (Siemens TimTrio); Nijmegen, the Netherlands (Siemens Skyra); Rome, Italy (GE, Signa HDxt); and Utrecht, the Netherlands (Phillips Medical System, Achieva/Ingenia CX)."
rci1_using_msad.location: Laidi2022.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Parcellation of Cerebellar Lobules

rci2_using_epd.detail: EU-AIMS LEAP dataset used as reference cohort for normative model training; LEAP is in the confirmed EPD list
rci2_using_epd.supporting_text: "We analyzed data from the EU-AIMS LEAP (18). This cohort is a large multicenter observational study, which aims to identify and validate stratification biomarkers in autism."

rci3_epd_name.detail: EU-AIMS LEAP (Longitudinal European Autism Project); control subjects from this cohort used as reference for normative model
rci3_epd_name.supporting_text: "A Gaussian process regression model was trained at each voxel in the control cohort using age, sex, site of inclusion, FSIQ and ICV as covariates to predict cerebellar grey matter volume."

rci5_n.detail: Training phase; all EU-AIMS LEAP control subjects (n=219) used; 10-fold cross-validation performed for model validation before retraining on entire control sample for predictions in ASD individuals
rci5_n.supporting_text: "Control Subjects, n = 219" / "we used 10-fold cross-validation in neurotypical individuals before retraining the model in the entire sample to make predictions in individuals with autism."
rci5_n.location: Laidi2022.pdf.md: Results / Table 1; 1-s2.0-S0006322322012781-mmc1.pdf.md: Supplementary Methods / Normative modeling analysis

rci6_sex.detail: Training phase; male N estimated from total N (219) × reported sex ratio (64% males) = 140 males; female N = 219 - 140 = 79
rci6_sex.supporting_text: "Sex Ratio (% of Males): 64%" for Control Subjects (n=219)

rci7_age.detail: Training phase; age in years; values reported as integers consistent with paper's precision
